newsitem.title: USA: Lucid sees few physical changes after space stay.
newsitem.headline: Lucid sees few physical changes after space stay.

text.p: U.S. astronaut Shannon Lucid said on Monday she was physically fit and in good health after a record 188 days orbiting the Earth, proving that long space flights were not harmful.

Lucid was in Washington to receive a Congressional Space Medal of Honour from President Bill Clinton on Monday, nine weeks after returning from her record stint performing scientific research on the Russian space station Mir.
"One thing that we learned from the space flight is that long duration space flights are a very doable thing," Lucid said on CNN's "Early Edition".
"Readjusting back to living on Earth was much easier than I had anticipated," she said.

Hours of daily exercise on a treadmill in the space station had helped to keep her fit, she said. "There was some calcium loss in the bones. But I had very good bones to start with, so my bones are still in very, very good shape and everybody was very happy," she said.
Her blood chemistry showed no significant changes. "There was nothing outside of the normal range in my blood when I got back as compared to pre-flight," she said.
Speaking on ABC-TV's "Good Morning America", Lucid said she preferred longer space flights to shorter trips because the pace of work was less hectic.
She said she was eager to work on the international space station, due to be built next year. "That would be really neat," she said.
